messages:
pagerbot: INCIDENT P1 — GPU pool 'prod-infer-1' saturated, queue depth 482, avg wait 14.2s. Auto-scaler triggered but new allocs not reaching Ready. Pager sent to eng-oncall.

mira: I'm on it. Seeing 5xx and spike in tail latencies on /v1/generate. App logs show RPC timeouts to modelserver.

kevin: checking HPA and node provisioning. running `kubectl get hpa -n inference` now.

jordan: I can see pool utilization graph — all 8 nodes at 100% GPU util. Warmup metrics show long readiness: avg GPU init 28s -> pod not Ready for ~30s.

kevin: HPA shows replicas increasing but pod startups stuck in ContainerCreating for ~25-40s. Output: ```NAME         TARGETS   MINPODS MAXPODS REPLICAS AGE
infer-hpa    95%/80%    2       50      18      6h```

mira: also seeing registry pull latencies in the same window. Hypothesis: registry throttling + long model warmup -> HPA tries to scale but pods slow to be usable -> queue grows.

jordan: logs from node-init: ```2026-03-17T10:12:05 startup: pulling image redistribution-worker: grpcio timeout after 18s
2026-03-17T10:12:35 nvidia-driver ready
2026-03-17T10:12:50 model load start``` Warmup ~35s.

kevin: Confirmed. Also noticed kubelet churn on 3 nodes around 10:11 UTC — kubelet restarted, caused pod restarts. Might be infra blip that amplified warmup problem.

sara: Immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to lower-cost, lower-latency model for non-SL queries 2) temporarily raise minReplicas for infer deployment to 12 3) mark the busiest customers and throttle non-critical jobs. I'll apply 1+2 now.

mira: +1 on fallback. How to route? opsbot, can you toggle route?

opsbot: ACTION: routing rule `fallback-lowlatency` enabled for route /v1/generate with priority header X-Redwood-Fallback. Affected requests ~28% of total.

kevin: Applied `kubectl scale deployment/infer --replicas=12 -n inference`. Starting to see new pods scheduled but a couple pending due to image pull concurrency limits.

jordan: Adding registry mirror for the model images would help. Tracking a quick mirror to pre-warm node images.

mira: Customer impact: ~12% increase in error budgets for hosted API during spike window 10:10–10:40 UTC. Notified support to queue priority tickets; churn metric shows SLO breach risk.

kevin: For the in-incident RCA notes: timeline so far — 10:08 UTC queue starts rising, 10:11 kubelet restarts on 3 nodes, 10:12 HPA triggers, 10:13 image pull latencies + model warmup ~30s, 10:15 fallback routing enabled, 10:18 scaled minReplicas -> pods scheduling, 10:30 queue begins to decline.

jordan: Evidence: paste of node logs and HPA metrics uploaded to the incident doc. Key log snippets: image pull timeouts, kubelet restarts, model load durations.

mira: Hypotheses to validate in RCA: 1) Image registry throttling caused slow container pulls -> increased pod startup time. 2) Kubelet restarts reduced available capacity transiently. 3) Model warmup time (35s) not accounted for in autoscaler project -> autoscaler reacts but latency persists.

kevin: Next actions post-incident: - add registry mirror & increase image pull concurrency - add readiness gating to avoid routing to pods until model is loaded - tune HPA to consider pending pod startup (maybe use a queue-length based scaler) - add GPU warmup metric to autoscaler heuristics.

sara: For immediate customer comms: drafting a status note summarizing impact and mitigation, ETA for full RCA EOD.

mira: handing this to kevin and jordan for full RCA and timeline build. I'll stay on slack for any followups. @kevin @jordan please ack.

kevin: ack — will own RCA writeup, pulling registry metrics and kubelet events.

jordan: ack — will dig into model warmup traces and pod startup histograms.

pagerbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — queue drained to normal thresholds, fallback routing remains until next deploy. Recording incident for RCA. :white_check_mark:
